title: Privileged identity & KMS compliance sync with Nova Genomics
customer_attendees: Dr. Elena Ruiz - Head of IT
summary: Customer wanted an end-to-end review of SSO (SAML) + SCIM provisioning flow and our RBAC model plus KMS/HSM options for encryption at rest and audit logging retention. Key topics: least-privilege role mapping, JIT and SCIM deprovisioning, private deployment options for EU data residency, audit log retention and integrity, and HSM-backed key management. Agreed next steps include sharing SOC2/ISO certs, a role-mapping template, and a 2-week pilot for SCIM sync + audit sampling.
action_items: Maya Chen: Share SOC2 Type II summary and ISO27001 certificate by 2026-07-23
Jordan Patel: Draft role-mapping template and least-privilege examples (3 roles) by 2026-07-26
Karim Ahmed: Provide current IdP metadata and SCIM attributes list by 2026-07-24
Priya Menon: Confirm pilot user group (10 engineers + 2 admins) by 2026-07-25
Maya Chen: Schedule pilot kickoff meeting for 2026-07-28
next_steps: Redwood to provision a 2-week SCIM + SAML pilot in Redwood Private in eu-west-1
Customer to send IdP metadata and SCIM attribute mapping
Redwood to enable audit-log snapshot exports for compliance sampling
Follow-up call after pilot week 1 to review logs and role behavior
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-21 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz (Nova Genomics Head of IT), Karim Ahmed (Security Architect), Priya Menon (Eng Manager)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Jordan and I from Redwood. Elena, Karim, Priya, can you hear us okay?
[00:06] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks. We wanted to go through the SSO/SCIM flows, and then dig into the key management and audit side, mostly for our compliance team.
[00:14] Jordan Patel: Great. Our plan — quick alignment on requirements, then walk through SAML config, SCIM provisioning/deprovisioning, RBAC patterns, and finally KMS/HSM options and audit log retention. Sound good?
[00:23] Priya Menon: Yep that's perfect. We have SOC2 Type II requirements and a planned ISO audit later this quarter, so timing is tight.
[00:32] Karim Ahmed: One big ask up front — we need proof of non-repudiation and tamper-evident logs. Also we aim to use our own KMS keys in HSM where possible.
[00:41] Maya Chen: Totally understood. We'll cover options — hosted, dedicated, private — and where customer-managed keys are supported.
[00:48] Jordan Patel: Alright jumping in. On SAML SSO, Redwood supports SAML 2.0 with SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows. We'll need your IdP metadata XML and attribute mappings (email, name, groups). For SCIM we support both SCIM v2 pushes and inbound provisioning from major IdPs.
[01:10] Karim Ahmed: For SCIM, does Redwood support incremental syncs and deprovisioning events rather than full list pulls? We want immediate revocation.
[01:18] Jordan Patel: Yes — SCIM push delta is supported. Deprovisioning can be immediate; we also support JIT provisioning for first-login use cases. Note: sometimes provisioning attributes get mangled depending on IdP — e.g., group names or role claims — so we recommend a canonical mapping step.
[01:35] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Can we restrict who can create service accounts? We don't want engineers creating high-privilege tokens.
[01:42] Jordan Patel: You can, we have RBAC with admin roles and scoped roles. Typical pattern is: 1) Admins manage role/SCIM mapping; 2) Engineers get scoped runtime roles (read-only or inference-only). We can show a role-mapping template.
[01:58] Priya Menon: Show us an example — we prefer least-privilege defaults.
[02:03] Jordan Patel: Sure. Example roles: platform-admin (deploy/model pinning), infra-ops (network/config), inference-runner (invoke endpoints only), billing-viewer (metrics/cost). Each role maps to specific SAML group or SCIM attribute.
[02:20] Priya Menon: What about ephemeral elevated access? We need JIT escalation for debugging for 1 hour.
[02:27] Jordan Patel: We support temporary role grants via our Console with time-limited roles or you can integrate with your privilege broker. It's not a full PAM but timebound elevations are possible and audit-logged.
[02:40] Karim Ahmed: On audit logs — what's the retention and integrity model? Our compliance wants append-only logs with export to our SIEM.
[02:48] Maya Chen: Audit logs capture token activity, admin actions, role grants, SCIM events, and SAML auths. We store logs in an immutable bucket for the duration you pick — default 90 days for hosted; for Private/Dedicated you can configure retention and forward to your SIEM via SSE or syslog.
[03:07] Jordan Patel: For integrity, we support signed log snapshots (SHA256 manifests) and can provide periodic signed digests you can verify. If you need HSM-backed signing for log manifests we can enable that in Private deployments.
[03:22] Dr. Elena Ruiz: That sounds promising. About encryption at rest — we want to use our KMS keys. Can Redwood accept external CMKs?
[03:29] Jordan Patel: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) via your cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM-backed keys in supported regions. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption but not always BYOK unless you're on a dedicated/private contract.
[03:45] Karim Ahmed: Is there an HSM integration lane? Our policy requires HSM for key storage for certain datasets.
[03:51] Jordan Patel: HSM-backed KMS is available in Private deployments. We have an HSM bridge for key signing and rotation workflows. Keys never leave your control; Redwood stores only wrapped keys.
[04:03] Priya Menon: Do keys rotate automatically? We need rotation logs for audit too.
[04:08] Jordan Patel: Rotation can be automated via your KMS policy or you can trigger rotations through our API. Rotation events are recorded in audit logs and visible in Console.
[04:19] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Data residency — our samples and derived features must remain in EU. Can we run inference and log storage in eu-west-1 only?
[04:26] Maya Chen: Yes. In Private we can deploy entirely in your VPC in eu-west-1. With Dedicated we can pin capacity to a region and ensure data egress controls. Hosted can be region-restricted for enterprise tenants but you'd want a Dedicated or Private for strict residency.
[04:44] Karim Ahmed: What about telemetry and traces? Do you send traces to Redwood cloud or can we keep them on-prem?
[04:50] Jordan Patel: Telemetry can be configured — sensitive traces can be suppressed or forwarded to your observability endpoint instead of Redwood. In Private deployment, traces stay in your environment.
[04:59] Dr. Elena Ruiz: One more on SAML: how do we handle multiple identity providers? We'll have partners with different IdPs.
[05:06] Jordan Patel: We support multiple IdPs via tenant mapping. You can have IdP A mapped to one group set and IdP B to another; SCIM configs can be per-IdP too. Some caution: group name collisions need canonicalization.
[05:20] Karim Ahmed: Are there known gotchas with SCIM attributes? Our Group -> Role mapping can be inconsistent depending on how the IdP handles nested groups.
[05:27] Jordan Patel: Yup, nested groups commonly cause mis-maps. We recommend flat group claims or a normalization layer. We'll send a mapping sheet that prescribes attribute names we consume.
[05:39] Maya Chen: Quick pause — Elena, Karim, is there a baseline access matrix you currently use?
[05:44] Dr. Elena Ruiz: We have an internal matrix but it's generic. Would appreciate a Redwood template that aligns Redwood roles to our matrix.
[05:51] Jordan Patel: We'll do that — the action item.
[05:55] [06:00] Priya Menon: On audit exports — can we pull logs to our SIEM every 24 hours or stream them?
[06:06] Jordan Patel: Both. We support bulk export snapshots (signed) daily and streaming via secure syslog/HTTPS to your endpoint. For high-volume events we recommend streaming to minimize delays.
[06:18] Karim Ahmed: For tamper-evidence, you mentioned signed manifests — what's the rotation of the signing key?
[06:25] Jordan Patel: Signing keys are rotated quarterly by default, and we can align rotation schedule with your compliance calendar. If you want, you can own the signing key in the HSM and we just use it to sign manifests.
[06:37] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Ok, let's talk about service account tokens and long lived keys. We can't have tokens that never expire.
[06:44] Jordan Patel: Agreed. Default token lifetimes are short — e.g., 1 hour for interactive and configurable for service accounts (recommended 24 hours). We support refresh tokens with limited scope and rotation. For service accounts you can use short-lived credentials obtained via a signed assertion from your token broker.
[06:59] Priya Menon: Do you support SCIM support for deprovisioning across multiple groups? Example: a contractor removed from two groups in the IdP should lose both sets of permissions in Redwood automatically.
[07:08] Jordan Patel: Yes, SCIM delta will pick that up if IdP sends correct remove operations. If IdP is slow, we recommend a periodic reconcile job.
[07:18] Karim Ahmed: For the pilot, we want to test deprovisioning, auditable role changes, and BYOK behavior. How long to spin up a Private pilot?
[07:26] Maya Chen: We can spin a constrained Private tenant in eu-west-1 in about 3-5 business days for a pilot, depending on legal/Kickoff and access to your IdP metadata and KMS info. Dedicated spin-up is faster but doesn't always provide BYOK.
[07:40] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Legal will need SOC2 evidence and a data processing addendum.
[07:46] Maya Chen: We'll share SOC2 Type II attestation and sample DPA — action item to send those.
[07:52] Jordan Patel: Quick note — sometimes the client's IdP SAML cert rotation causes short outages for SP-initiated logins. We recommend setting overlap window and notifying us during rotations.
[08:03] Priya Menon: Good callout.
[08:07] [08:30] Karim Ahmed: On encryption in transit, we need mTLS for internal control plane calls. Is that supported?
[08:36] Jordan Patel: mTLS is supported for Private deployments and Dedicated peering. Hosted uses TLS with mutual auth options for certain endpoints. We can provide the cert rotation docs.
[08:47] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Any compliance stories from other genomic customers? Just to know if there were tricky things.
[08:53] Maya Chen: We had a biotech customer require air-gapped evaluation for a specific workflow; they ended up using our Private package with HSM and per-tenant logging exports. The main friction was around network egress rules and KMS access — but once keys were provisioned it was straightforward.
[09:08] Priya Menon: Ok that's helpful.
[09:12] Jordan Patel: For the pilot scope: SCIM delta provisioning, SAML SSO with your IdP, role mapping for three roles (admin, infra, inference), audit export streaming to your SIEM, and testing BYOK in a wrapped-key flow.
[09:27] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Timeline — we want pilot live within two weeks. Is that realistic?
[09:31] Maya Chen: If we get IdP metadata and KMS ARN today, yes we'd aim for a 7–10 business day window.
[09:39] Karim Ahmed: I'll get the metadata and a short list of sample users.
[09:43] Priya Menon: We'll pick the pilot cohort.
[09:46] [10:00] Maya Chen: Anything else on compliance? ISO controls mapping maybe?
[10:05] Dr. Elena Ruiz: If you have an ISO control matrix mapping for how Redwood satisfies common ISO 27001 control families, that'd be great.
[10:12] Maya Chen: We'll include an ISO mapping doc.
[10:16] Jordan Patel: Last technical nuance — SCIM attribute names we consume: userName, externalId, active, groups[] and you can include custom claims like role_hint. We'll send a template CSV.
[10:29] Priya Menon: Thanks. One more — token revocation propagation time. If we revoke a token server-side, how fast is enforcement across the fleet?
[10:36] Jordan Patel: Tokens are checked against an authorization cache with TTL; default propagation under 60 seconds for Dedicated/Private; hosted could be up to 2 minutes depending on caching config. We can tune TTL for the pilot.
[10:50] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Great.
[10:53] Maya Chen: Let's capture action items and next steps — recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO docs, role mapping template, and spin up pilot once we have metadata and KMS details. Pilot kickoff 2026-07-28 tentative. Follow-up call after week 1 of pilot.
[11:12] Karim Ahmed: Sounds good. We'll aim to have metadata by 2026-07-24.
[11:16] Priya Menon: I'll confirm the cohort by 2026-07-25.
[11:20] Maya Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll share the packet and calendar invite after this.
[11:24] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Thanks, appreciate it.
[11:27] [End of call]

Notes on transcription: small mis-hearings around product names (Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as "Redwood Dedicate") and some timestamps clipped. Some technical acronyms (HSM, KMS, SCIM) occasionally expanded inconsistently.
